title: Coin Dash
shows: A small, complete game: title screen, settings with rebindable keys, timed rounds, a pause and a saved best time (kept in the browser's storage).
controls: Arrow keys or WASD move. Enter starts, Escape pauses, Q goes back to the title, O opens the settings.

title: Ember Hop
shows: A second complete game: a platformer through two cave levels from the Tiled editor, with physics, prefabs, particles, streamed music, a following camera and saves at the braziers.
controls: Arrow keys or A/D move, Space jumps, X throws a flare, Esc pauses; Enter starts a run, C continues. A gamepad works too.

title: Tutorial: Crab Cove
shows: The finished game of the 2D tutorial: a Tiled level with solid tiles, coins, water, a flag, sound, a title screen and a saved best score.
controls: Arrow keys or A/D walk, Space jumps; on the title screen, click a button or pick one with Tab or the arrows and press Enter.

title: Battle
shows: Two armies of 10,000 units marching on shared flow fields and fighting, with a spatial grid for targeting and seeded randomness.
controls: Click to set red's rally point; drag with the right button to pan, scroll to zoom. A attacks, D defends, Space pauses, 1 to 3 set the speed, R restarts.

title: Flow fields
shows: 20,000 agents following one shared flow field around walls and through mud, recomputed when the goal moves.
controls: Click to move the goal; drag with the right button to pan, scroll to zoom. H shows the distance field, Space pauses.

title: Ant colonies
shows: Ants forage and lay pheromone trails: a spatial grid, a field shared by every ant, systems at reduced rates and entities taking turns.
controls: Drag with the right button to pan, scroll to zoom. Space pauses, Period steps, 1 to 4 set the speed.

title: Boids
shows: Flocking (separation, alignment and cohesion) with a spatial grid for the neighbour search.
controls: Space pauses, Period steps, 1 to 4 set the speed.

title: Bunnymark (ECS)
shows: Bouncing sprites stored as entities and drawn by the built-in sprite system: a stress test for sprite batching.
controls: Hold the left mouse button to add 1,000 crabs per frame.

title: Sprites
shows: Drawing sprites: position, rotation, scale, tint, draw order and pivot.
controls: Arrow keys or WASD move the big crab; the small one follows the mouse.

title: Sprite effects
shows: Sprite blend modes and sprite shaders: an additive glow, an outline and a dissolve.
controls: Move the mouse: the glow under it is an immediate draw with additive blending.

title: 2D particles
shows: A campfire of smoke, fire and sparks around a sprite, a glowing trail and bursts: emitters sorted among the sprites.
controls: Move the mouse for the trail; click for a burst of confetti.

title: 2D lights
shows: A dark tile dungeon lit by wandering coloured lights with shadows from the walls and crates, normal-mapped tiles and a lantern that follows the mouse.
controls: Move the mouse to aim the lantern. L adds a hundred more lights, N switches the normal maps.

title: Tilemap
shows: A million-tile map with animated sprites on it; only the tiles in view are drawn.
controls: Drag with the right or middle button to pan, scroll to zoom; left click paints stone.

title: 2D physics
shows: Crates, balls and rocks fall, stack, bounce and slide down a ramp, with a sensor in the bucket.
controls: Left click drops a crate, right click a ball, middle click a rock; Space blasts everything near the mouse away, R starts over.

title: Tiled level
shows: A level from the Tiled map editor: parallax clouds, animated water, coins placed as objects and colliders made from the tiles.
controls: Left and right arrows walk, Space jumps. Left click builds walls (an autotile rule), right click knocks them down.

title: Editor playground
shows: The editor in the runtime inspector: pause the game, then select, move, duplicate and place entities, with undo; Play and Stop restore the scene.
controls: Press ` (backquote) to open the inspector, then Pause. Click a crab to select it and drag to move it; right-drag pans, the wheel zooms.

title: Camera, text and UI
shows: A 2D camera, shapes, text and buttons in one small scene.
controls: Drag with the right or middle button to pan, scroll to zoom; click the world to drop a crab. The buttons follow the orbiting crab or reset the camera.

title: UI: a shop
shows: Retained UI: an item grid that scrolls, a text input, a toggle and a modal confirmation dialog.
controls: Pick an item, then buy it; Tab and the arrow keys move the focus.

title: UI: a settings menu
shows: A settings menu operated by keyboard and mouse, with named controls for screen readers on the desktop.
controls: Tab and the arrow keys move the focus, Enter presses, Escape closes the dialog.

title: Shard Grove
shows: The complete 3D game: a glTF level and skinned glTF characters with animation state machines, a character controller, enemies that chase on a navigation mesh, positional sound, lights and shadows, menus, a HUD, a sign in the world, quality presets and saves at the shrines.
controls: WASD or the arrow keys move, Q and E turn the view, Space jumps, F pulses, Esc pauses; the menus take the mouse or Tab and Enter. A gamepad works too.

title: 3D scene
shows: Meshes, materials, a sun with shadows and hundreds of instanced models spinning.
controls: Drag with the left button to orbit, scroll to zoom; Space pauses the spinning.

title: Tutorial: Lantern Yard
shows: The finished game of the 3D tutorial: a glTF yard that is drawn and solid, a character controller, a following camera, lights, crates and a HUD.
controls: WASD or the arrow keys move, Q and E turn, Space jumps. A gamepad works too.

title: Many lights
shows: A dark scene lit by a hundred coloured point and spot lights.
controls: Watch: the lights move by themselves.

title: Terrain
shows: Heightfield terrain drawn coarser with distance, with grass, dirt and rock blended by a weight map, a lake and an underwater effect.
controls: WASD moves, Q and E go down and up, the arrows turn, U switches the underwater effect.

title: Material shaders
shows: Custom material shaders (a lake with waves, grass in the wind, a procedural pattern) with post-processing.
controls: Left and right arrows turn the time of day, F switches the fog.

title: Streaming landscape
shows: An endless landscape streamed in around a flying camera: terrain tiles built as jobs, uploaded a couple a frame and freed once far behind.
controls: The camera flies by itself; the arrows steer, W and S change speed, Q and E go down and up.

title: Skinned meshes
shows: Procedural tentacles on skeletons, posed every frame; on WebGL2 the skinning runs on the CPU.
controls: Watch: the tentacles sway by themselves.

title: 3D particles
shows: A billboard particle emitter: a cone of additive sparks with gravity, drag and colour over their life.
controls: Watch: the emitter runs by itself.

title: Trails and lines
shows: A ribbon trail behind an orbiting ball, lines and decals.
controls: Watch: the ball flies by itself.

title: UI in the 3D world
shows: Retained UI drawn on a panel in the 3D world, aimed at with the middle of the screen.
controls: Click to press the button in the middle of the view.

title: Depth of field
shows: A target effect: the lit frame copied into a small render target and blended back in for a cheap depth of field.
controls: Watch: the camera stays put.

title: 3D physics
shows: First-person walking over hilly terrain: a character controller that climbs steps, and crates to push over.
controls: Click to lock the mouse (Escape lets it go). The mouse looks, WASD walks, Shift runs, Space jumps; click shoves the crate you look at.

title: Vehicle
shows: A box car on four raycast wheels driving over hilly terrain.
controls: W accelerates, S brakes and reverses, A and D steer, Space is the handbrake, R puts the car back on its wheels.

title: Compute: rain on a pond
shows: A wave simulation in a compute pass on the GPU every frame, read by the water's shader to bend its normals.
controls: Click the water to drop a stone in.

title: Compute: eye adaptation
shows: A compute pass that measures how bright each frame is and keeps a running average, so the picture settles as the sun rises and sets.
controls: Watch: the sun moves by itself.
